problem: Existing open-vocabulary scene graphs / video-language memories are mostly 2D and frame-local, or need RGB-D/IMU/SLAM, and lack a shared upright metric frame, so direction, distance and visibility relations become inconsistent across views and long horizons.
motivation: AR assistants and robots need a persistent, queryable spatial memory built from cheap casual egocentric RGB video. Grounding objects in metric structural anchors (walls, doors, windows) gives interpretable relational queries and fast retrieval without dense mapping.
key_idea: Reconstruct a metric-aligned upright 3D scaffold from RGB video with a feed-forward geometry model, then build a rooted memory tree of anchors, objects and two-layer text descriptions, so relational retrieval and navigation-style guidance become graph walks.
insight: Explicit metric anchoring plus stable scene-level descriptions gives robust step-wise guidance and hierarchical retrieval. The ablation on Scene 2 shows that removing the two-layer descriptions drops SR_nav from 0.79 to 0.72 and Acc_path from 0.69 to 0.62. Scale perturbation of ±10% degrades performance only mildly (NE 3.7→3.9/4.1). Overall accuracy is mostly on par with the best VLM baseline (Gemini 2.5 Flash), not clearly better, so the gain is mainly in step completion and speed.
method: 3D environment preparation: VGGT (swappable with SLAM3R/COLMAP) estimates poses and dense depth from RGB, fused into a point cloud; floor-plane fitting aligns +z, heading is stabilized, and a floor-to-ceiling height prior sets metric scale.

Structural anchors: walls (large vertical planes) and doors/windows (thin openings) are proposed, verified across views, merged, and kept only if stable (point support, multi-view coverage, temporal persistence); optional SpatialLM seeds coarse boxes.
Hierarchical memory tree: Root → Level-1 anchors → Level-2 open-vocabulary objects (3D boxes plus multi-view crops/masks/embeddings) → Level-3 descriptions; typed edges (near/attached/left-of).

Metric relational semantics: vertical predicates (on/over/under) are computed by heuristics in the z-aligned frame; lateral relations are kept as view-local tags and consolidated to allocentric only when cross-view evidence is consistent.

Two-layer descriptions: an image-level layer (view-specific attributes and relations) and a scene-level layer promoted conservatively after multi-view agreement, used as the default reference for retrieval and guidance.

Low-latency query: an index by node type and 3D region; locate and relational queries walk the tree with distance/orientation/visibility checks; an instruction is converted into anchor/object waypoints for step-wise offline guidance on a decision-point graph.

setting.backbone: VGGT geometry back-end + open-vocabulary detection/segmentation + LLM/VLM for text (frozen, off-the-shelf; the specific LLM is not stated)
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB video (LUCI pin camera, 0.5–1 Hz sampling), no depth/IMU
setting.action_space: none (offline navigation-style guidance over predefined decision points on a 2D floor-projected graph; no active control)
setting.simulator: none; recorded video of a Replica scene plus two real-world scenes
setting.privileged: manually verified decision-point reference map and human-verified ground truth; height prior for metric scale; offline prebuilt memory from the whole recorded sequence

numbers_note: All benchmarks are the authors' own 3-scene evaluations (one Replica scene, two self-captured), so none map to a canonical benchmark. Split 'test' is a placeholder. The ablation table (Scene 2) reports slightly different numbers for the Full model than the main table (SR_nav 0.79 vs 0.80, SR_obj 0.79 vs 0.78, Loc@path 0.65 vs 0.66).
results: SpatialMem is roughly on par with the strongest baseline, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and beats the open-source and GPT-4o baselines. In Scene 1 it has the best StepComp (0.89 vs 0.84), SPL (0.69 vs 0.68), NE (3.1 vs 3.2) and SR_obj (0.83 vs 0.81), but slightly lower SR_nav (0.77 vs 0.78) and Acc_rel (0.84 vs 0.86). Performance degrades moderately in the cluttered Scene 3 (SR_nav 0.54, NE 4.6, which is worse than Gemini's 4.0), and the method has lower test-time latency.
limitations: Proof-of-concept on only three scenes (one Replica, two self-captured) with an offline memory and a manually verified decision-point map; navigation is not closed-loop control and no public navigation benchmark is used.
Baselines are only 2D VLMs; no stronger 3D-aware baselines. Gains over Gemini are marginal and some metrics (Scene 3 NE, door accuracy, Loc@path) are worse.
Fine-grained details (shelf levels, small objects) and lateral relations under clutter are weak; heuristic thresholds and a height prior for scale are used.
